name: Pol Pot
role: Leader of the Khmer Rouge and de facto ruler of Democratic Kampuchea (1975-1979)
summary: Pol Pot led the Communist Party of Kampuchea and ran Democratic Kampuchea, a one-party state that emptied the cities, abolished money, markets and religion, and collectivised agriculture under the Four-Year Plan. His own speeches stress independence and self-reliance, class struggle, and armed revolution; he saw Vietnam as the chief threat and purged party members as agents. Estimates of deaths under his rule run to 1.5-2 million.

sources.title: Democratic Kampuchea
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of the regime's policies: the expulsion of Vietnamese, the suppression of minorities, the single official language and the state's control of the economy

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 1977 speech claims a state-run health network: a hospital with nurses and a pharmacist for every 100 cooperative families, medical care assured to all, no payment (money abolished). Stated as achievement; actual provision was poor.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Abolished markets, money and private trade; the state and cooperatives collected and distributed all products; said collective work succeeds and individualistic work 'leads inevitably to failure'.

public-ownership.rationale: Led a regime that abolished private property and placed the economy under state and collective ownership, with the state running factories, trade and exports.

property-fundamental.rationale: Speech sets the aim of 'gradually eliminating the idea of private ownership'; his government collectivised all private property, including tools, land and household goods.

worker-ownership.rationale: Speech presents cooperative members as 'true masters' of land and harvests who direct and manage their cooperatives, but in practice the party and state controlled them and industry was state-run.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: cadres were told to watch for enemy agents and lifestyle meetings enforced constant mutual vigilance; this implies tolerance of surveillance, but no statement addresses surveillance directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Speech boasts of wiping out 'social diseases and addictions' as an achievement.

state-harmful.rationale: Built and defended a state with 'worker and peasant state power' and said it should be strengthened; no sign of anti-statism.

empower-police-military.rationale: Gave top priority to national defence and a large army and security apparatus (about 200 prisons).

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Speech lists prostitution among 'decadent remnants' and says it was 'completely wiped out'.

decide-locally.rationale: Rule by the party centre and democratic centralism, though zones and cooperatives had practical autonomy and he credited cooperative self-management.

rehabilitation.rationale: Speech distinguishes re-educating 'contradictions among the people' from eradicating hard-core enemies; S-21 and the security centres tortured and executed rather than rehabilitated.

traditional-family.rationale: Policy deliberately broke up the traditional family: communal eating, separated families, mass weddings arranged by the party.

more-religion-public.rationale: His regime abolished religion, closed pagodas and mosques and banned religious practice.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Condemned the old society's 'corrupt and depraved culture and traditions' and abolished traditional culture, yet praised Khmer heritage and Angkor.

gradual-change.rationale: Called for 'great leaps' and building socialism 'better and faster'; society was transformed at once.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Expelled ethnic Vietnamese and closed the borders, which the record describes as reducing foreign presence.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Made 'independence, sovereignty, self-reliance' the core principle and rejected outside control.

free-trade.rationale: Foreign trade was a state monopoly with the state collecting products and exporting them, mainly to China and friendly states.

nation-first.rationale: Core line of 'independence, initiative and self-reliance' and defending 'sovereignty and territorial integrity'.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: from his absolute stance on sovereignty and non-interference.

open-borders.rationale: Ran a largely closed country; in 1978 interview said it would welcome only 'friends'.

limit-growth.rationale: Planned production by 'leaps and bounds' and rapid growth.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred: he credited hydraulic works, medicine and technical training for solving the country's food and health problems, but not technology in general.

revolution-justified.rationale: Speech justifies 'revolutionary violence' and armed struggle as the highest form of struggle.

experts-over-public.rationale: Stressed reliance on 'our people' and trained technicians 'from the ground up' in place of existing experts, whom the regime persecuted.

central-planning.rationale: Presented and drove the Four-Year Plan (1977-80) setting national production quotas (three tons of rice per hectare) with the state organising output, distribution and exports; rejected markets.

socialized-markets.rationale: His government abolished domestic markets and money rather than operating them under public ownership; in 1978 he said the future of currency depended on 'the people', leaving a hedge.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Plan used rice-export surplus, directed by the state, to build industry; 'we take agriculture as the basis and use its fruits to build industry'.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Abolished private property in land, tools and possessions in favour of collective cooperatives and the state.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolished money, markets and wages in 1975; the 1977 speech celebrates operating 'without the use of money, with no daily salary'. In 1978 he said return of currency depended on the people.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Abolished money entirely, which goes beyond the statement's market direction; he never addressed central banks or a market-set currency.

one-party-rule.rationale: As secretary of the CPK he ruled a one-party state; the speech credits 'the correct and clear-sighted leadership of the Party' for everything.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Speech condemns feudalists and kings as exploiters; his regime abolished the monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Rejected multiparty elections and ruled a one-party state; he said the party would be rejected if it betrayed the people.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: the cooperatives and workers' collectives were the organising units of the regime, but no statement names workers' councils as the basis of power.

political-violence-never.rationale: Speech endorses revolutionary armed violence; he ordered killings of political enemies.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said that the people's wartime struggle tempered their courage and patriotism, without saying war builds national character as such.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts, police, army and security centres were all run by the party-state.

military-superiority.rationale: Said the army must defend the country and that Democratic Kampuchea would defeat Vietnamese aggression, which is not an aim of military superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Regime favoured ethnic Khmers, expelled ethnic Vietnamese in 1975 and persecuted other minorities; he spoke of the 'race of Cambodia'.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Speech presents Cambodian history as class struggle through slave, feudal and capitalist eras alongside national struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: 1978 interview: aspiration is a society of 'happiness, prosperity and equality for all' with no exploiting and exploited class; his regime enforced uniform clothing, rations and labour.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Speech condemns individualism and aims to remove 'the idea of private ownership'.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Speech: collective work succeeds and individualism fails; the individual's old attitudes must be reshaped for the collective.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred: nature was treated as a resource for the revolution's production targets, with no statement that it has value in itself.

limit-population.rationale: Speech: 'We have no reason to reduce our population or to level it off'; aim to rise from nearly 8 million to 15-20 million within ten years.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Planned rapid industrialisation using agricultural surplus.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pursued rapid transformation with 'great leaps and bounds' in agriculture, hydraulic projects and industry, even where it disrupted existing institutions.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rejected the old society though invoking Angkor-era glory; revolution was the stated aim.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred: the Party insisted on a 'correct line' based on revolutionary principle, and judged policy by ideological fit as well as results.

direct-action.rationale: Speech: after rigged elections in 1955 and 1958 the party took up armed struggle in place of electoral politics.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Speech calls abolishing money and communal living 'a successful step' toward resolving the contradictions between city and countryside, workers and peasants, manual workers and intellectuals.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Speech describes a communal support system with no wages in which all are 'basically assured of all needs'; distribution by rationed supply, not by work or wealth.

production-for-use.rationale: The economy was run without markets or profit; production aimed at rice for people, army and export to fund state construction.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Speech describes peasants and workers as exploited by landlords, merchants and capitalists, and says the revolution's substance is eliminating exploiting classes.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Speech applies 'the dictatorship of the proletariat' to the small group of reactionary elements (OCR text of the speech partly garbled); his state held worker-peasant power over the former ruling classes.

collective-farming.rationale: Drove forced collectivisation; the speech praises the cooperatives (700-1,000 families) and says individualistic work leads to failure.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Attributed aggression and war to imperialism and the exploiting classes, describing the US as leader of world imperialism.

conscription.rationale: All able-bodied people were mobilised for 'production and national defence' and the army was drawn from the cooperatives.

total-state.rationale: The party-state directed economy, education, culture, family life and religion; the speech sets 'socialist construction in all areas'.

national-rebirth.rationale: Aimed to rebuild a 'new Kampuchea' purged of the old society's decadent remnants, 'more glorious than Angkor'.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Speech: 'We don't want even one inch of anyone else's land'; but Khmer Rouge forces raided Vietnamese territory.

single-common-good.rationale: Inferred: he defined one revolutionary line and the people's interest through the Party, rather than balancing the competing interests of groups.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education was run by the party and state and tied to production; normal schooling and private schooling abolished.

national-self-determination.rationale: Speech: Cambodians as 'masters of their own country' and 'deciding our own destiny'.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred: the regime used force against Vietnam and Thailand-facing enemies without seeking any outside authorisation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Presented Marxism-Leninism and historical materialism as the scientific guide to the revolution, while rejecting religion.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Everyone who could work was required to labour in the cooperatives in return for food and shelter.

class-collaboration.rationale: Speech centres the elimination of exploiting classes; the regime persecuted capitalists, landlords and 'new people'.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Closed schools, universities and pagodas and abolished traditional culture for the revolution.

dominated-front.rationale: Speech calls on non-aligned and third-world countries to unite against imperialist and expansionist great powers.

workers-nation.rationale: His revolution was organised on national lines under independence and self-reliance, ethnic Khmer nationalism marking the party.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described the old state as an instrument of feudal and capitalist ruling classes, to be replaced by a workers' and peasants' state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The Plan pursued agriculture and hydropower rather than fossil fuels, and no statement addresses domestic oil, gas or coal production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Forced minorities including the Cham and Chinese to adopt Khmer language and customs and broke up their separate communities.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His government directed every area of life: economy, culture, education, family.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Divided the population into 'new people' and base people, classified enemies by class and ethnicity, and massacred them (Cham, Vietnamese, officials).

socialism-one-country.rationale: Claimed to have built socialism in Kampuchea alone on self-reliance, though noting solidarity with others.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Schools were run by the party and taught production and 'revolutionary patriotism', with religion banned.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Speech says the worker-peasant state must be defended and strengthened against foreign enemies; no withering away is sought.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said the people would decide whether the society was on the right path and could decide differently if unsatisfied, though the Party held power regardless.

trade-surplus.rationale: Said the regime exported rice and rubber to pay for imported machinery and industrial goods, which it treated as necessary for independence.

population-transfer.rationale: Ethnic Vietnamese were expelled en masse in 1975 and the Cham forcibly dispersed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Speech affirms 'revolutionary violence' and says the CPK began armed struggle in 1968 and attacked the enemy first.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Condemned competition among individuals and cooperatives as producing corruption and individualism, and said the competition was only for money.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Allowed only the Party to rule, banned other parties, and treated opposition parties as enemies to be eradicated.

separated-powers.rationale: All power rested in the party centre and standing committee, with no independent checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Speech: the people must have 'the leadership of a true party of the working class with a correct line'.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Speech names poor and lower-middle peasants (75% of the population) as the base whom the revolution serves; 'workers and peasants must benefit most' (1978).

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Said Kampuchea had no reason to reduce or level off its population and should increase it as quickly as possible.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred: he treated minority groups as enemies of the nation, but no statement claims diversity weakens cohesion in general.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: the regime appointed cadres through the Party and did not use lottery or election for offices.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Ordered arrests, torture and executions of alleged internal enemies without legal process (e.g. S-21), which he defended as measures 'to defend ourselves'.

party-controls-media.rationale: State and party controlled all media: only the DK radio and party press existed, and no non-revolutionary entertainment was allowed.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Revolutionary Army acted 'under the leadership of the Communist Party'; he was party secretary directing military policy.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Cadres, soldiers and workers had no salary in the regime, which he presented as collective equality.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Speech praises democratic centralism and party discipline; he purged members who dissented.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Insisted on independence and sovereignty as non-negotiable and rejected any union that would dissolve Kampuchean sovereignty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: No non-revolutionary entertainment allowed and traditional culture banned.

people-in-arms.rationale: Speech praises people's war and mobilising the whole people for defence.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Emptied the cities to abolish urban living; speech counts the city-countryside divide a contradiction to be overcome in favour of agriculture.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Said the old education, copied from foreign systems, was incapable of serving the country and that technicians trained from the base served better than graduates.

death-penalty.rationale: Records show mass executions of those branded traitors; he said enemies must be 'eradicated'. The executions followed no real trials.

minority-language-support.rationale: Cham were forbidden to use their own language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Cham Muslims were forbidden to practise Islam or speak their language, with no exemptions for religious minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The regime enforced uniform black clothing, collective living and conformity of everyday life.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Speech argues Cambodia was not truly independent before 1975 because its economy and culture were dominated by imperialism, and that socialist transformation of production relations followed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Pursued the Four-Year Plan's production targets through total coercion, though the speech's stated reason for repression was defence and revolution rather than growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred: the regime rejected foreign aid and investment as a basis for development, and called for self-reliance.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Abolished private property in favour of collective ownership for the common good, which goes beyond the statement's limited justification.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Denounced the Vietnamese as annexationists and swallowers of territory, and said their occupation of Kampuchean land was unlawful.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Closed religious institutions, converted pagodas to other uses and set monks to labour.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Abolished the monarchy and called it the enemy of the people and of religion, rejecting sacred rulership.

character-from-environment.rationale: Speech says people carry 'vestiges of our old class character', fixable through education and collective life.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: the regime's leaders ruled by Party decree with no legal limits, but no statement addresses a ruler being above law.

leader-cult.rationale: He told Thayer he never sought to publicise himself ('I don't want to tell people that I'm a leader'); the regime ruled in the name of anonymous 'Angkar'.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Speech says antagonistic contradictions with enemy agents persist after 1975 and that a party that stops representing the exploited 'changes its class nature'; he purged party members as traitors.

land-redistribution.rationale: Speech endorses peasants driving out landlords who had seized their land and the elimination of landlords as a class; land then went to cooperatives, not individual farmers.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The regime raised Kampuchea Krom as a historical grievance but did not claim territory on the basis of nationality in its public statements.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: he presented Vietnam's Indochina Federation as an unacceptable union and rejected political union of neighbouring peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Denied minority groups self-governing cultural institutions and schools, banned their languages and dispersed their communities.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Speech uses stages of historical materialism and cites production relations, but also stresses will, line and mass consciousness.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Cooperatives designed to be as self-sufficient as possible and the country to rely on its own forces, though the state traded with China and other friendly states.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: he rejected foreign trade and foreign influence, but no statement addresses binding labour or environmental standards in trade agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: Production relied on revolutionary enthusiasm and communal duty in place of wages; speech credits 'dedication' and 'sacrifice' and notes no daily salary.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Speech recounts launching armed struggle in 1968 with few rifles, rather than waiting for conditions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Condemned feudal aristocracy and abolished privileged classes.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Presented the nation's own history and traditions as the basis of education, but the statement about school history is not addressed directly.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Speech condemns colonialism and imperialism as plunder.

patriotic-education.rationale: Speech: children, youth, workers and soldiers receive 'education in revolutionary patriotism'.

delink-world-market.rationale: Policy of self-reliance and a largely closed economy with state-controlled trade, mainly with China; 1978 interview still had state exports of rice to import goods.

elective-rulers.rationale: The 1976 election was a single-list vote under the Party, so the regime held an election but did not choose rulers competitively.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1976 National Assembly was a one-party body under the Party, so parliament was not the supreme authority in practice.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Required everyone to take part in collective political life, including criticism and self-criticism sessions, and rejected withdrawal from public affairs.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Argued that the old culture served the exploiting classes but gave no account of mass culture pacifying the people.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Said poor countries had been plundered and oppressed by foreign imperialists, feudalists and colonialists, and that independence was needed to end it.

party-own-road.rationale: Speech: 'A line copied from others will not work'; the party must decide its own destiny, and he broke with Vietnam's party.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Repeated principle of 'independence, sovereignty, self-reliance'; the speech says the country relied on 'our own resources' and 'bare hands', with rice exports funding development.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Contested: he said the present borders were the product of foreign annexations but pledged to defend them and denied claiming former territories (1978), while also raising the loss of Kampuchea Krom.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said Cambodia had no model, chose its own line and rejected copying others.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: the army was described as defending the Party's revolution and the constitution, but no statement gives it a guardian role over civilian government.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: In the Plan's explanation he refused foreign investors, saying they would bring political entanglement, and aimed to keep the economy in national hands.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private land ownership abolished and land worked collectively by cooperatives under the state.

single-official-language.rationale: Only Khmer was tolerated; Cham forbidden to speak their language. No stated language policy by him.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Condemned individual accumulation and the pursuit of money and possessions as corrupting, and collectivised households in the cooperatives.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Refused foreign investment and aid because they would bring political entanglement, so foreign influence was restricted.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Said the population should grow to 15-20 million, but gave no financial incentives, so the mechanism is not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Compulsory labour in the cooperatives gave everyone work, though not framed as an employer-of-last-resort guarantee.

non-intervention.rationale: Speech: Democratic Kampuchea does not interfere in others' affairs and will never allow anyone to interfere with it or alter its borders. Said Vietnam's pressure violated this.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Told Thayer the Vietnamese had agents inside the leadership and a coup committee; mostly aimed at the Vietnamese state, with ethnic Vietnamese persecuted.

local-production.rationale: Each cooperative and region was to run its own workshops and use local raw materials; factories were built on 'locally available raw materials'.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Said foreign policy and independence were stipulated in the constitution, and that Kampuchea would decide its own destiny.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Told Yugoslav journalists Cambodia 'cannot accept being slaves to Vietnam'.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: In 1976 everyone had to bring private possessions, even kitchen utensils, to be used collectively.

religion-illusion.rationale: Said the problem of religion had been solved by itself as material conditions changed, though he did not describe religion as an illusion.

socialized-care.rationale: Communal dining and a communal supply system took over household provision.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Speech describes each cooperative as 'a small collectivist society' with common property and communal living; the party, not the communities, ultimately directed them.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the regime moved and dispersed populations for its own purposes rather than encouraging majority settlement, though policy of settlement is not addressed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He was a communist who called his party Marxist-Leninist and his state socialist.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: he cited Kampuchea's historical borders and the lost islands as a legal and historical basis, which is a limited form of historical claim.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Banned all opposition and independent organisations; arrested and executed suspected enemies; spoke of 'eradicating' the 'smallest possible number' of persistent opponents.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Speech condemns colonial exploitation of Cambodia.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Said the people should take part directly in decisions in workplaces and communities through the mass line and democratic centralism.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Monks and people were ordered to wear peasant black clothing and the uniform dress of the cooperatives, and religious dress was banned.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Built and prioritised a large army.

rich-first.rationale: Stated aim: a society with no rich and no poor, no exploiters or exploited, with equality for all.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Declared 'independence, sovereignty, neutrality and nonalignment', though in practice he relied on China.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: the regime refused foreign loans and investment with political conditions, which is in line with refusing lender conditions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: the regime targeted Chinese merchants and traders as exploiters associated with capitalism, which fits a policy of boycotting minority shops.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Courts found a policy of 'establishing an atheistic' society, banning religious practice; the evidence is of suppression rather than classroom teaching of atheism.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: he rejected foreign influence and interference, but no statement addresses foreign bases on national territory.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Pay was abolished and supply was given by collective work; the statement's contrast with ownership is only loosely reflected.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Led an armed struggle and told Thayer the party had to 'defend ourselves'.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Speech traces a continuous 2,000-year struggle of the nation and invokes Angkor.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Speech and national anthem honour the 'sublime blood' of those who fell and says the revolution must repay them.

culture-before-state.rationale: The speeches give culture an important role, but no statement sets cultural renewal before state building.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Claimed his state was 'worker and peasant power', though the party held actual power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Water works, hospitals and local services were run by the state and cooperatives as collective services.

person-over-state.rationale: Forced evacuation, forced labour, mass weddings and executions treated people as means to state ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Presented politics as the cultivation of the people's material and moral life, without stating that people have a spiritual nature.

dense-cities.rationale: Evacuated the populations of Phnom Penh and other cities to the countryside, and treated cities as a source of enemy power and corruption.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: the regime treated ethnic minorities as enemies rather than as groups with legitimate political interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: he spoke of the 'race' and national honour of Kampuchea and defended national pride, but not racial pride as such.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Said Democratic Kampuchea would never aggress against anyone, yet launched border attacks on Vietnam in 1977-78.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Speech says foreign imperialists aim at 'weakening our country and reconquering it'; he says Vietnam planned to 'swallow' Cambodia.

capital-controls.rationale: Kept the economy closed to foreign capital and tightly controlled the movement of money and foreign exchange through the state.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the Party's army and militia were the armed forces, though armed guerrilla units were also raised in the countryside.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the army was disciplined under the Party and required to fight the enemies it was assigned, with no provision for refusal.

smash-state-machine.rationale: His forces overthrew the Lon Nol state and abolished its institutions, army and courts rather than taking them over.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: the Plan measured natural resources in production and export targets, but did not frame them as capital valued in the economy.

sacred-nation.rationale: National anthem and speech call the soil and independence 'sacred'.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: aimed to remake people through re-education and communal life into 'revolutionary proletarian' persons.

workers-own-party.rationale: Said the working class needed its own party to lead the revolution, which the Communist Party of Kampuchea claimed to be.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Required minorities to adopt the Khmer language and customs and banned their own languages.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: the regime suppressed all religion rather than granting equal recognition to several interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Said everyone wanted democratic freedoms but that they had belonged to the exploiters, and presented the regime's own rule as the genuine form of freedom.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1976 constitution declared equality of men and women, but votes and offices were controlled by the party.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Land and resources were collectively or state owned.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Said a socialist state with nationalised property and a planned economy must be defended against capitalist restoration and foreign attack.

national-church-status.rationale: Abolished Buddhism's traditional status and treated monks as a parasitic class.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Ended the autonomy of minority regions and dispersed their people into cooperatives, according to the record.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Insisted on the borders Vietnam had recognised in 1966-67 and defended 'present borders'.

simple-living.rationale: Enforced austerity and self-sufficiency, uniform clothing and communal living.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: he framed the defence of the nation's territory and ancestors' struggles as a sacred duty, without a stated spiritual bond to the land.

close-ties-china.rationale: Relied on China for aid, arms and trade; DK's only major patron.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Held the lands, forests, rivers and resources in common through the state and cooperatives, with individual appropriation eliminated.

self-ownership.rationale: Imposed forced labour, forced marriage and forced relocation on the population.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: he combined modern technical training with national tradition, such as local medicine and traditional methods.

national-resource-control.rationale: Said the country's resources and economy must be under the Kampuchean people's own control, independent of foreign interests.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Speech joins revolutionary patriotism with serving workers and peasants.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: A communist party led his state, but it abolished markets and money rather than building a market economy within socialism.

notes:
Based on the 1977 speech, a 1978 interview and the 1997 Thayer interview, plus the record of measures he drove. The Four-Year Plan text and Revolutionary Flag articles were not opened; their content is known here only through DC-Cam's description. The speech text is an OCR scan with a few garbled passages. He later denied responsibility for Tuol Sleng, which the scholarly record contradicts.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 79 answers taken from it, 111 agreed, 4 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Positions are drawn from his speeches and interviews (1976-1978, compiled in Pol Pot Selected Works, Volume 1, and the Four-Year Plan documents) and from the record of policies he drove, described secondhand in Wikipedia and in the Yale volume's introductions. His 1997 interview with Nate Thayer is known only through news summaries; the 1976 constitution's text was not opened, and its provisions are taken from secondhand summaries. Most of the statement list is not addressed by his speeches or the record and is answered null. Atrocities (S-21, the purges, the expulsion of Vietnamese, the killing of Cham and Chinese) are recorded in the secondhand sources and are not presented as his stated views, but they are the record of policies he personally drove and are reflected in the answers where a statement matches.
